result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.edge_dfs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Traverse every edge reachable from a source in depth-first order. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L44007-L44058){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.edge_dfs( source=None, orientation=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Edge DFS](/assets/graphs/edge-dfs.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The directed triangle A to B to C to A plus a fourth edge A to C, searched depth-first from A (outlined). The numbered accent arrows give the visit order: the search dives A to B, B to C and C back to A, then takes the remaining edge A to C fourth. The card lists the four edges beside dfs_edges, which keeps only (A, B) and (B, C)." width="100%"} The depth-first counterpart of `edge_bfs()`: every edge reachable from the source is visited exactly once, following each new edge as deep as possible before backtracking. This is the traversal NetworkX's `find_cycle` builds on, and it suits Euler-style walks and edge-by-edge exploration of directed graphs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, list, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A start node, a list of start nodes, or `None` (default) for all nodes, in ID order. [orientation]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : `None` (default), `"original"`, `"reverse"` or `"ignore"`, as in `edge_bfs()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The edges in visit order as `(u, v, edge_id)` triples, with a fourth `"forward"`/`"reverse"` element when `orientation` is given. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist or `orientation` is invalid. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Iterative depth-first search over edges with a per-node edge iterator. $O(V + E)$. Matches NetworkX's `edge_dfs`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#99b4a49d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("A", "C")]) [(g.get_label_from_id(u), g.get_label_from_id(v)) for u, v, _ in g.edge_dfs("A")] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [('A', 'B'), ('B', 'C'), ('C', 'A'), ('A', 'C')] ``` ::: :::
